name: Add charts to infrastructure
description:
1. Task: add monitoring charts to the Infrastructure view, reusing the same chart library as the analytics charts.
2. Analysis: `DailyChart.vue` uses `chart.js/auto`; `useInfra.js` exposes only a snapshot endpoint (`/api/infra/summary`) with a fixed 5s poll and `autoRefresh: false` (no history API).
3. Created `useInfraMonitor.js`: live flag defaulting to `true`, refresh-interval selector defaulting to `5s`, and a 120-sample rolling client buffer with a poll loop kept separate from the shared store.
4. Created `MonitoringChart.vue` (generic Chart.js wrapper matching `DailyChart` palette/typography) and `MonitoringPanel.vue` (KPI tiles with peaks/averages, host-load / container-state / docker-resource charts, rule-based "Possible problems", busiest containers).
5. Updated `InfraView.vue`: Monitoring tab prepended, interval selector beside the Live toggle wired to the monitor, filters hidden on that route, and start/stop sampling on mount/unmount — no duplicate polling.

/**
 * ============================================================================
 * codx-junior — Infrastructure (Docker) API module
 * File: src/api/modules/infra.js
 * ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * BACKEND CONTRACT
 * ----------------
 * Thin HTTP client for the infrastructure REST API under `/api/infra/*`,
 * implemented by `api/codx/junior/api/infra.py`.
 *
 * Every request goes through the regular `API.get/post/put/delete` helpers, so
 * authentication (cookie/bearer), base URL and interceptors all apply.
 *
 * All routes are gated server-side to users with the `admin` role: container
 * start/stop/kill, container creation, host registration, SSH key management,
 * cloud provisioning and any prune/removal are privileged operations. A
 * non-admin caller receives `403`.

 * HOSTS ARE THE ROOT OF THE TREE
 * ------------------------------
 * Every resource endpoint is scoped by `?host=<InfraHost.id>`, so the UI reads
 * `GET /api/infra/hosts` FIRST and sends the selected id on all the following

 * SSH KEYS ARE NOT HOST SCOPED

 * A key pair must exist BEFORE the machine it unlocks: cloud provisioning

 * collection (`/api/infra/ssh-keys/:id`) and hosts point at one via

/**
 * ============================================================================
 * Infrastructure — live monitoring samples + refresh scheduler.
 * ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * The Docker API exposes a *snapshot* (`GET /api/infra/summary`), not a history
 * series, so the charts are fed from a rolling buffer sampled on the client:
 * every refresh appends ONE point, the oldest one is dropped once the buffer is
 * full. That keeps the graphs honest — nothing is interpolated or invented — and
 * it needs no backend change.
 *
 * WHY A SEPARATE MODULE
 * ---------------------
 * `useInfra.js` owns the Docker snapshot, the tabs and every action. This module
 * only owns the *time* dimension (how often we poll, and what we remember), so a
 * chart can be added or dropped without touching the shared store.
 *
 * LIVE BY DEFAULT
 * ---------------
 * `monitoring.live` starts as `true`: the Infrastructure view is a monitoring
 * surface, so polling is the expected behaviour as soon as it mounts. Polling is
 * still stopped on unmount (`stopMonitoring`) and resumed on the next mount, so
 * the preference survives navigation while no timer burns in the background.
 * ============================================================================
 */
import { computed, reactive, watch } from 'vue'
import { state, loadAll } from './useInfra'

/** Intervals offered by the header selector (seconds). */
export const REFRESH_INTERVALS = [
  { value: 2, label: '2s' },
  { value: 5, label: '5s' },
  { value: 10, label: '10s' },
  { value: 30, label: '30s' },
  { value: 60, label: '1 min' }
]

/** Requested default: refresh every 5 seconds. */
export const DEFAULT_REFRESH_SECONDS = 5

/**
 * Samples kept in memory. At the default 5s cadence 120 points span ~10 minutes
 * — long enough to spot a spike, short enough to stay readable in one chart.
 */
export const MONITORING_MAX_SAMPLES = 120

/**
 * The tab descriptor lives here (not in `useInfra.TABS`) because the store is
 * shared by every infra panel and is not the owner of the charts.
 */
export const MONITORING_TAB = { id: 'monitoring', label: 'Monitoring', icon: 'fa-chart-line' }

export const monitoring = reactive({
  live: true,
  interval: DEFAULT_REFRESH_SECONDS,
  samples: []
})

let timer = null

/* ── Helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
